title: Holo Sticker
description: Your artwork as a die-cut holographic foil sticker with a peeling corner, rendered with three.js and tilting toward the pointer.

props.name: src
props.description: The artwork: an SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP URL (a data URL works too). Transparent areas are cut away.

props.name: alt
props.description: Describes the artwork; without it the sticker is decorative (aria-hidden).

props.name: settings
props.description: Any dial: finish, size, border, cutTolerance, overlay, ink, relief, layers, holoIntensity, bands, hueShift, grain, pattern, peelDirection, peelAmount, curl, shadow, light.

props.name: tilt
props.description: A fixed tilt from -1 to 1 on each axis, for stills.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Replaces the static picture shown without WebGL 2 or under reduced motion.

a11y: With alt it is role="img" with that name; without it the sticker is decorative.
Without WebGL 2, under reduced motion and before the first frame it shows a static picture: the artwork with a die-cut edge and a foil sheen.
Pointer tilt only changes the picture; nothing needs a pointer to read or use.
usage: <HoloSticker src="/logo.svg" alt="Our logo as a foil sticker" className="size-64" />
docs:
Installed `HoloSticker` and its three.js renderer in `components/ui/`, plus the `render-loop` helper in `lib/`. Render `<HoloSticker src="/logo.svg" alt="Our logo" className="size-64" />`; the canvas fills the box, so size it with `className`.

Tune any dial with `settings`, for example `settings={{ finish: "chrome", peelAmount: 0 }}`. Rendering pauses off screen and in hidden tabs; without WebGL 2 or under reduced motion a static picture of the artwork shows instead.

Needs `three` (installed) and, for TypeScript, `@types/three`. Ported from jal-co/holosticker (MIT, copyright 2026 Justin Levine); the license text is in each file.
